items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section XIII, List of Answers on Terminology 5:1
items.html: It is known that the light of Hochma is called yesh and its concealment is called ayin. But the subject here is the aspect of the returning surrounding light, which goes out and enters through the correction of the hairs of the head and the beard. Hence the head of the Avir is called by the name ayin, for it is the power of the screen of Atik that brings out the three heads of Arich Anpin from the aspect of the primordial Hochma (Inner Observation, Page 436, Item 1), which is called the membrane of the Avir, and it is what causes the exit of the first three of Hochma in the aspect of a returning surrounding light, as the Rav wrote above (Part 1, Page 348, Item 117) that the hairs come out from the power of the membrane of the Avir. For upon the departure of the returning surrounding light from the head, the hairs are made — which are the reflected lights that clothe this light — into the aspect of the waste of the brain, for the light that they clothed has departed, and they no longer have anything to clothe there by which they could remain there within the Mochin; hence they go out of the vessels of the head in the aspects of hairs, as is known. Thus the hairs and the returning surrounding light, namely the concealment of the primordial Hochma — all this comes from the membrane of the Avir. Hence Mocha deAvira is called by the name ayin, for ayin depends on it, since all the concealment of Hochma comes from it. But the head of Atik is also called ayin, by way of borrowing, because this membrane of the Avir is truly the aspect of the screen of the Malchut of the head of Atik; only since it does not rule over the first three of the Galgalta, its power begins at the membrane of the Avir, as is known. And since the Malchut of the head of Atik is the root of the membrane of the Avir, it too is called ayin. But the principal name is in Mocha deAvira, for the rule of this screen is not revealed except from the membrane of the Avir and below. (Part 1, Page 369, Item 158; Part 1, Page 371, Item 161).
